claims.text: The trip deviated, and the deviation is measured on the trace. EV-GPS-00503 gives trace_distance_km of 6.81 km between the recorded pickup (Serangoon Garden Circus, started 16:26:40) and the recorded dropoff (Bishan MRT, ended 16:55:40), against a booked optimal of 4.2 km on the trip record. That is an excess of 2.61 km, or 62.14% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 establishment tests pass: the excess exceeds 0.8 km absolute and exceeds 20% of optimal. POL-RD-01 is explicit that where gps_trace.trace_distance_km and trip_record.actual_distance_km disagree, the trace figure governs and the rounded 6.8 km convenience copy on the trip record may not be cited for the threshold test, so the excess stands at 2.61 km.

The trace that carries that excess is clean for policy purposes. EV-GPS-00503 has 175 fixes at a 10 s cadence against an expected 10 s interval, coverage_pct 100.0, an empty gaps array and max_gap_sec 0.0. No limb of POL-RD-07(a) to (c) fires: there is no gap over 90 seconds, no straight-line jump over 500 m and no sustained interval above 30 seconds. The excess therefore stands at the measured figure, no independent corroboration is required, and POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged.

The excess is not merely established, it is additionally MATERIAL: 62.14% of optimal is above the 50% materiality figure in POL-RD-01. That triggers the driver_profile check in POL-RD-06, which I run on the two fields that clause names and no others: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 250, so no repeat pattern is established and no uplift under POL-RD-06(b) is available on this record. The finding of deviation rests, as POL-RD-06 requires, on this trip's own trace and not on the profile; the profile is used only for the test POL-RD-06 sets and it yields nothing either way.

The driver's explanation does not excuse a metre of it. His answer is that 'the app gave me that route' and that the rider should 'complain to the company' — that is not a traffic event and it is not a clause. Read charitably as an external-cause assertion, POL-RD-13 tests it against the traffic_advisory for this trip and nothing else; the bundle's advisory artifact EV-ADVIS-00503-01 is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0, its issue detail recording that 'no advisory covers Serangoon Garden Way or Ang Mo Kio Ave 3 in this window'. The POL-RD-03 comparison cannot be run on the record, POL-RD-03 is unavailable, the assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08, and the driver's excuse supplies neither a reduced excess nor an amended optimal. Nothing in this policy exonerates a driver for following his navigation.

Nor can the driver say the detour was requested. The chat log for this trip is empty: message_count 0, no messages, first and last message timestamps null. There is no rider instruction to test, no timestamped message, no named road and no waypoint_hint for the POL-RD-04 corroboration test to use. POL-RD-04 is simply unavailable on this record, and the rider cannot have asked for a turn into an industrial estate he was told nothing about at the time.

The remaining exculpatory routes are closed on the face of the trip record. POL-RD-05 needs an amended endpoint: pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null and amended_optimal_distance_km is null, so the endpoints booked are the endpoints driven and no recomputation against an amended optimal is open to the driver. POL-RD-11 needs an upfront-quoted fare: fare_model is METERED and quoted_fare_sgd is null, so its bar on distance-and-time refunds does not apply and POL-RD-02 governs. POL-RD-12 needs a pooled trip: vehicle_type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, and solo_optimal_distance_km is null, so the baseline is the 4.2 km booked optimal and is not rebased to any matched itinerary.

The rider has carried his burden and the driver has not carried his. Under POL-RD-08 the rider must show the artifacts describe the same trip and that the excess meets the POL-RD-01 threshold on an unimpaired trace: trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry TRP-00503 with consistent pickup and trip timestamps, and the trace is unimpaired, as set out above. The burden then shifts to the driver to point to a specific artifact and a specific clause, and he points to none — his own statement concedes the route 'looked odd' while disclaiming responsibility for it. The rider's profile does not add any corroboration requirement either: deviation_claims_60d is 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so the additional-corroboration condition in POL-RD-08 is not met.

The refund is arithmetic, not discretion. Under POL-RD-02 on this METERED fare: recomputed_fare = ((3.80 base + 0.75 x 4.2 optimal km + 0.28 x 7.5 optimal min) x the surge_multiplier read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier, which is 1.0) + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 ERP on the optimal route + 0.00 fixed surcharges + 0.00 waiting time - 0.00 promo = (3.80 + 3.15 + 2.10 + 0.80) = 9.85. Charged_total was 17.82, so the refund is 17.82 - 9.85 = 7.97, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05 as 8.00. That is far above the 0.50 de minimis floor, and at 44.7% of the charge it is well short of the 90% share that would convert it to a full refund, so the correct remedy is a partial refund of SGD 8.00 with charged_total, recomputed_fare and refund stated on separate lines.

Nothing is added on top and nothing is counted twice. The fare carries no ERP lines at all — erp_gantries is empty and the ERP total is 0.00 — and no airport surcharge, since a trip ending at Bishan MRT does not originate at an airport. There is therefore no pass-through correction to make under POL-RD-09 and no risk of the double count that POL-RD-09(1) forbids: the 8.00 is confined to the distance and time charges the rider was overcharged for, and every component of it traces to a line of the fare breakdown.

Finally, the shape of the outcome matters. This dispute was filed by the rider, and the fare breakdown shows payment_status CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.00. Under POL-GEN-03 the only outcome that leaves the rider not carrying the disputed charge is money moving back to him: a partial refund of 8.00. NO_ACTION would leave a rider who does this route every week paying 17.82 for a ride that took 29 minutes over 6.8 km against a 7.5-minute, 4.2 km optimal route through an industrial estate he never asked to visit.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and to the driver: this trip is decided on the recorded numbers, and both of you end up in nearly the same place on them.

The deviation is ESTABLISHED. The trace EV-GPS-00503 shows 6.81 km between the recorded pickup (Serangoon Garden Circus, 16:26:40) and the recorded dropoff (Bishan MRT, 16:55:40), against a booked optimal of 4.2 km on the trip record EV-TRIP-00503 (optimal duration 7.5 min, optimal route source routing-engine-v3.2). The excess is 2.61 km, or 62.1% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 tests pass (over 0.8 km absolute and over 20% of optimal), and 62.1% is also above the 50% materiality line, so the POL-RD-06 driver-profile check was run. As POL-RD-01 requires, the trace figure governs over the rounded 6.8 km convenience copy on the trip record. The trace is clean for policy purposes (175 fixes at a 10 s cadence, coverage 100%, empty gaps array, max_gap_sec 0.0), so no limb of POL-RD-07(a)-(c) fires and no independent corroboration is needed.

No exculpatory clause applies, and I have said so explicitly where a clause required me to. There is no chat log for this trip at all (EV-CHAT-00503, message_count 0), so the rider-requested-detour test under POL-RD-04 cannot be run on the record and the clause is unavailable; no rider instruction, road name or waypoint_hint exists to corroborate. The endpoints were not amended (pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are null, amended_optimal_distance_km null), so POL-RD-05 does not apply. The fare is METERED with quoted_fare_sgd null, so POL-RD-11 does not bar a distance-and-time refund. The vehicle is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12 does not rebase the optimal to a matched itinerary. The driver's explanation that he was only following the navigation is not a clause, cites no artifact, and names no traffic advisory; under POL-RD-08 an assertion citing no evidence ID carries no weight, so it neither reduces the excess nor supplies an amended optimal. The bundle does contain a traffic advisory, EV-ADVIS-00503-01, but it is MISSING (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT, 'no advisory covers Serangoon Garden Way or Ang Mo Kio Ave 3 in this window'); it carries no fact, the driver did not cite it in support of any clause, and POL-RD-10(5) is therefore not engaged.

The refund is arithmetic, not discretionary. Under POL-RD-02 on this METERED fare: recomputed_fare = 3.80 base fare + 0.75 x 4.2 optimal km (3.15) + 0.28 x 7.5 optimal min (2.10) = 9.05, multiplied by the surge multiplier of 1.0 read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier (the field this policy puts it on), plus 0.80 platform fee, plus 0.00 ERP on the optimal route, plus 0.00 fixed surcharges, plus 0.00 waiting-time fee, less 0.00 promo discount = 9.85. Charged_total was 17.82, so the refund is 17.82 - 9.85 = 7.97, rounded UP to the nearest SGD 0.05, that is SGD 8.00. That is well above the 0.50 de minimis, and at 44.7% of the charge it is short of the 90% share that would convert the remedy to a full refund. The outcome is therefore PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 8.00 to the rider.

Nothing is added on top and nothing is counted twice. POL-RD-09 supplies no standalone correction: erp_gantries is empty and tolls_erp is 0.00, there is no airport surcharge on a trip that neither originates at an airport nor ends at one, and waiting_time_fee and promo_discount are both 0.00. The driver's brief is also right that every charged line reconciles to the trip record (base 3.80, distance 6.8 km x 0.75 = 5.10, time 29.0 min x 0.28 = 8.12, platform fee 0.80, total 17.82), so POL-RD-10(8) is not engaged.

No repeat-deviation pattern is established: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0, below the 3 the clause requires, and 0 over completed_trips_90d of 250 is a ratio of 0.000, below the 0.05 the clause also allows; no POL-RD-06(b) full-refund uplift and no POL-RD-06(c) driver-conduct referral therefore follow, and no billing-integrity referral under POL-RD-09(4) arises because there is no unmatched charge line. The lifetime prior_deviation_flags counter mentioned in the driver's brief is a near-synonym of the trailing-window field: it is context only under POL-GEN-01, it was not used as a ground, and the finding of deviation rests on this trip's own trace alone. The disputed fare of 17.82 is only partly refunded; the balance, 9.82, stands as correctly charged.

Where the trace figure (6.81 km) and the trip record's rounded copy (6.8 km) differ, POL-RD-01 makes the trace figure govern, so the 2.61 km stands.

The trace is not impaired. EV-GPS-00503 carries 175 fixes at a 10-second cadence, 100% coverage, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0 seconds, so nothing in POL-RD-07(a) to (c) fires, no corroboration beyond the trace is required, and POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged. The missing traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00503-01 (status MISSING, weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT) carries no fact about this trip either way.

The driver's answer — that the app chose the road — is not an exculpatory clause and reduces no part of the excess. To the extent it is read as an external traffic cause, POL-RD-03 could only be run against a traffic advisory for this trip, and no advisory is on file covering Serangoon Garden Way or Ang Mo Kio Ave 3 in this window, so that comparison cannot be made and the assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor, and at 44.7% of the charged total it is below the 90% share that would convert it to a full refund, so the outcome is a partial refund of SGD 8.00. The remaining SGD 9.82 stands.

The rider's profile does not add any corroboration requirement either: deviation_claims_60d is 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so the additional-corroboration condition in POL-RD-08 is not met.

The refund is arithmetic, not discretion. Under POL-RD-02 on this METERED fare: recomputed_fare = ((3.80 base + 0.75 x 4.2 optimal km + 0.28 x 7.5 optimal min) x the surge_multiplier read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier, which is 1.0) + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 ERP on the optimal route + 0.00 fixed surcharges + 0.00 waiting time - 0.00 promo = (3.80 + 3.15 + 2.10 + 0.80) = 9.85. Charged_total was 17.82, so the refund is 17.82 - 9.85 = 7.97, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05 as 8.00. That is far above the 0.50 de minimis floor, and at 44.7% of the charge it is well short of the 90% share that would convert it to a full refund, so the correct remedy is a partial refund of SGD 8.00 with charged_total, recomputed_fare and refund stated on separate lines.

Nothing is added on top and nothing is counted twice. The fare carries no ERP lines at all — erp_gantries is empty and the ERP total is 0.00 — and no airport surcharge, since a trip ending at Bishan MRT does not originate at an airport. There is therefore no pass-through correction to make under POL-RD-09 and no risk of the double count that POL-RD-09(1) forbids: the 8.00 is confined to the distance and time charges the rider was overcharged for, and every component of it traces to a line of the fare breakdown.

Finally, the shape of the outcome matters. This dispute was filed by the rider, and the fare breakdown shows payment_status CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.00. Under POL-GEN-03 the only outcome that leaves the rider not carrying the disputed charge is money moving back to him: a partial refund of 8.00. NO_ACTION would leave a rider who does this route every week paying 17.82 for a ride that took 29 minutes over 6.8 km against a 7.5-minute, 4.2 km optimal route through an industrial estate he never asked to visit.

The refund on this trip is arithmetic, not discretionary: fare_breakdown.fare_model is METERED, so POL-RD-02 fixes recomputed_fare at ((3.80 base + 0.75 x 4.2 optimal km + 0.28 x 7.5 optimal min) x surge_multiplier 1.0, read from the fare_breakdown, which is where this policy puts the multiplier) + 0.80 platform fee + 0 ERP and tolls, which is 9.85. The refund is therefore charged_total 17.82 less 9.85 = 7.97, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05, that is SGD 8.00. The rider's contested figure of 17.82 is more than double the clause's own output and cannot be awarded on these figures.

FULL_REFUND is not open on this record: the refund of 7.97 is 44.7% of the 17.82 charged, well below the 90% share that POL-RD-02 requires before a full refund is substituted for the partial. The outcome for the filing party is therefore at most PARTIAL_REFUND as POL-GEN-03 defines it, and the balance of the charge is left standing.
